adversarial_refutations.argument:
NOT REFUTED. Round-2 adversarial check of CV:lem:piececurve (row 143, bundle CV.PieceCurveData, statement file work/reviews/cv-piece-reviewer-input-statement.lean.txt l.637-724) against d1_setup.tex 592-610 (+ def:piecediagram 565-590 for the datum), with the focus on `rotation_system`.

1. Expansion of `rotation_system` (l.716-721) to primitives. `pieceShadow hn hD hS H` (l.494-496) := `geoCarrierShadow hn (CarrierGeometry.ofDiagrammatic hD) _ (pieceCarrier …)` = `Shadow.single ⟨geoCornerCount …, _, geoCornerPolygon (S ∪ K_H) q_H⟩` (SM/GeoPositiveLift.lean:84-86, 97-99), and `geoCornerPolygon (S ∪ K_H) q_H` is `pieceCurve hD hS H` (l.460-462) by definition. `Strand = Σ i : Fin 1, ZMod k` (SM/LinkDiagram.lean:96); `dir s = edge (comp s.1).P s.2` (LinkDiagram.lean:106; `single_dir` 1636 is rfl), i.e. `dir s = pieceCurve (s.2+1) - pieceCurve s.2` (SM/Polygon.lean:49). `Crossing` = an unordered pair of non-adjacent strands whose closed segments meet (LinkDiagram.lean:246-251), `x.val` has exactly two strands (284), `crossingPoint x` a common point (372-376, unique under Generic 415-431). On the parent side `c.val` is the two-element set of remote parent edges (SM.crossing_card_two, used at l.605; `Crosses.isCrossing` CV/Setup.lean:516-519 shows the shape) and `edge P i = P (i+1) - P i`. So the field literally says: for every survivor c ∈ H and the double point x of C_H at crossingPoint c, there is a bijection of the two polygon edges of C_H through x with the two parent edges {i,j} of c such that each edge of C_H is a positive multiple of its parent edge.

2. Why the direction form determines the printed counter-clockwise half-edge order (d1:580-585; proof d1:664-666). `closed_plane_curve` (l.677) gives `(pieceShadow).Generic` (LinkDiagram.lean:394-399): `transverse` (det ≠ 0 for meeting non-adjacent strands) and `tail_off`, whence `Generic.crossingPoint_mem_interior` (LinkDiagram.lean:456-460): the crossing point is interior to both strands, so the four half-edges of C_H at x are the in/out halves of the two straight strands, i.e. rays in directions -dir s1, dir s1, -dir s2, dir s2. With `dir s = t_s • edge P (e s)`, t_s > 0, the four rays are positive rescalings of the parent's four rays -edge P i, edge P i, -edge P j, edge P j at c (the parent crossing is transverse by Diagrammatic clause 3, CV/Setup.lean:1382-1388 `det (edge P i) (edge P j) ≠ 0`), and det(dir s1, dir s2) = t1·t2·det(edge P i, edge P j) has the parent's sign. The cyclic counter-clockwise order of four rays is a function of their directions, so under the labelling (strand, in/out) ↦ (parent edge e s, in/out) the ccw order at x equals the parent's at c: exactly "the carrier's, which is the parent's" (d1:664-666), restricted to c ∈ H. The existential `∃ e` is harmless: e is unique, since two distinct strands of x are transverse (LinkDiagram.lean:291-300 + Generic.transverse) and so cannot both be positive multiples of one parent edge. The literal "sub-half-edge containment" reading (each half-edge of C_H a subsegment of the parent's half-edge) is TRUE in the library (GeoBlockInterior / geoCornerPolygon_block, SM/GeoPositiveLift.lean:129-133, SM/GeoCornerPolygon.lean:323-345) but is a strictly stronger geometric statement; the printed datum is the combinatorial ccw order of arc labels, which the direction form already fixes. Not needed for fidelity.

3. What remains unstated (all non-blocking, none a printed conclusion without a field). (a) The compatibility of e with the word's visit identification — that the strand e⁻¹(i) is the one on which C_H traverses the parent visit (c,i) — is not a field; it is the library block structure (`GeoBlockInterior.visit_edge` GeoPositiveLift.lean:160-168, `geoCornerPolygon_edge_smul` GeoCornerPolygon.lean:400-404, `geo_carrier_crossingPoint_parameters` GeoCarrierSelfIntersections.lean:457-461) and is the same trace convention as reading R-c (Gauss word of C_H = `carrierGaussList` filtered to H, l.689-694, the accepted CV.carrierword vocabulary, CV/CarrierWord.lean:126-127, 291-329). The printed "re-expressed in the restricted word's arc labels" is a relabelling determined by the word, so nothing printed is lost. (b) The relation between `rotation_system`'s x and `realizable`'s e (l.700-703) is consistent: for each c ∈ H, x := e.symm ⟨c,_⟩ has crossingPoint x = crossingPoint c, and any other x' with the same point would give two parent crossings at one point, excluded by Diagrammatic.

4. Reading R-b (binding of C_H by Classical.choose over `exists_pieceSupport`, l.351-356, 372-373, 396-397, rather than by the recursion): I verified the reviewers' extensional claim. For any spec K let K_q = {d ∈ K : some visit of d is owned by q at S ∪ K}. Since ρ_T = ρ ∘ selectedMarkPerm T differs between T = S ∪ K and T = S ∪ K_q only at visits of K \ K_q (SM/FlatCarriersDefs.lean:235-255), none of which lie on q's cycle, q's cycle and its true-corner list (367-369, 396-404) are identical at S ∪ K_q, so the corner polygon is unchanged; and K_q is route-reachable by reverse induction: at S ∪ K_q \ {d} both visits of d lie on the carrier of H (independence forces smoothing d to split, so at S ∪ K_q they lie on two different cycles, one of them q), so d is a double point of the current carrier of H outside H, and the carrier of H only grows as elements are removed. Hence Lean's C_H is always an outcome of the printed route (whose choice of d is equally free, d1:642). Non-blocking; a missing reachability clause, not a different object.

Every other field re-checked against 592-610: `carriers_of_S` (l.650) = "the |S|+1 carriers of S"; `initial_carrier` (653-655) = "the one carrier that carries H, unique by lem:carriers(iv)" and "H lies on one carrier before the iteration begins"; `step` (659-662) and `step_well_defined` (665-668) = "smoothing at each step one double point outside H and keeping the daughter curve that carries H, which Step 5 shows is well defined", universally quantified (stronger; "daughter" containment follows from accepted `carrierword_refines`, CV/CarrierWord.lean:226-229); `terminal` (671-673) = the end of the iteration (StepInvariant at K_H, q_H owns H); `closed_plane_curve` (677) = "a closed plane curve" (stronger: Regular ∧ Generic); `double_points` (680-685) = "double points exactly the crossings of H" in both combinatorial (geoCarrierCrossings q_H = H, FlatCarriersDefs.lean:451-454) and geometric form (GeoIsSelfIntersection, GeoCarrierSelfIntersections.lean:430-433, via geo_self_intersections 763-767); `gauss_word` (689-694) = "Gauss word … the parent word restricted to H in the parent's cyclic order" (linear lists both cut at P's vertex 0, implies the cyclic statement; plus GeoInheritsMarkOrder / TracedSuccessor at S ∪ K_H, SM/GeoCarrierCount.lean:564-568, SM/FlatCarriers.lean:3147); `realizable` (700-703) = "that restricted word is realizable" (crossing-point-preserving bijection, stronger than the round-1 Nonempty); `rotation_system` = the second half of the datum. Round-2 refutation attempt of CV:lem:piececurve (row 143, CV.piececurve / CV.PieceCurveData, statement file lines 637-725) against d1_setup.tex 592-610 (proof 611-667 read only for object names), expanding every field to primitives in the permitted modules. No blocking discrepancy found; every reviewer-flagged item re-checked and confirmed non-blocking. Findings:

1. Terminal binding by choice (R-b). exists_pieceSupport (351-356) specifies K by: S ∪ K ∈ Ind, K ∩ H = ∅, K ⊆ U(S), geoCarrierCrossings (S∪K) q = H, q owns all visits of H, GeoInheritsMarkOrder; pieceSupport/pieceCarrier are Classical.choose of it (372-373, 396-397). The printed C_H is 'the curve the proof's own route constructs' with free choice of d at each step (d1:642 'If C has a double point d outside K, smooth it'), so the printed C_H is itself determined only up to that choice. I verified the extensional claim the reviewers rely on, with the primitives: (a) every e ∈ K is non-adjacent to all of S ∪ K_i for K_i ⊆ K (S∪K ∈ Ind, Events.lean:186-188), so by lem:carriers (iii) both visits of e lie on one carrier at every intermediate stage; (b) if that carrier is the H-carrier, e is a legitimate route step (mem_geoCarrierCrossings, FlatCarriersDefs.lean:451-454); (c) otherwise smoothing e changes ρ = geoSmoothingSuccessor only at e's two visits (FlatCarriersDefs.lean:235-237), leaving the H-carrier's mark cycle, its IsTrueCorner marks (369) and hence geoCornerPolygon (402-404) unchanged; (d) elements of type (c) never become double points of the H-carrier (carriers refine), so K_route := the type-(b) elements is a terminal route outcome with the same pieceCurve. Conversely every route outcome satisfies the spec. So the set of Lean outcomes equals the set of printed outcomes; the meta-sentence 'the construction and not a description of its result' (d1:605) is respected in substance: the spec pins C_H to a smoothing-produced carrier, not to an arbitrary realization of the word. Non-blocking.

2. gauss_word (689-694). carrierGaussList is BY DEFINITION (CarrierWord.lean:126-127, 290-292) P's mark list filtered by ownership with vertices dropped, and carrierGaussList_eq_filter (176-178) makes conjunct 3 equivalent to 'every visit of H is owned by q_H', i.e. to terminal.2 (672-673) — it carries no order information by itself. The order content is conjuncts 1-2: GeoInheritsMarkOrder (GeoCarrierCount.lean:564-568: next mark of q in Γ's order = ρ a) and TracedSuccessor (ρ of the i-th list entry is the (i+1)-th, CarrierWord.lean:91-92, 221-222). Since the geo carrier curve is defined as the ρ-trace (geoCarrierTrace/GeoIsCarrierParameter, GeoCarrierSelfIntersections.lean:419-433), this states that the carrier curve meets Γ's marked points — in particular the two visits of each c ∈ H — in Γ's cyclic order, which is exactly how the printed proof itself reads 'the carrier's Gauss word' (d1:627-632 via lem:carrierword; accepted convention of row 137, CarrierWordData.carrier_word 312-316). The identification of the ρ-trace with the corner polygon pieceCurve (whose vertices are the true corners in inherited order, geoCornerPolygon_apply GeoCornerPolygon.lean:186-189) is accepted library content (U2b/U2c/U4), not a field: non-blocking (R-c).

3. realizable (700-703) and rotation_system (716-721). pieceShadow = Shadow.single of the corner polygon (GeoPositiveLift.lean:91-99; pieceDiagram_comp rfl at 751-752), so dir s = edge pieceCurve s.2 (LinkDiagram.lean:106, 1636-1637). realizable gives a crossing-point-preserving bijection shadow.Crossing ≃ H, so for every c ∈ H there is an x at crossingPoint c and rotation_system is never vacuous; crossingPoint is injective on Crossing P (GeometricVisits.lean:25-27), so distinct c give distinct double points. rotation_system's direction form (dir s = t • edge P (e s), t > 0, bijection strands ≃ parent edges, at the same point) fixes the four half-edge rays at x to be P's four rays at c, hence the same counter-clockwise half-edge order — the printed second half of the datum exactly as the printed proof argues it (d1:664-666). The 'sub-half-edge containment' reading is a stronger form and is NOT needed for fidelity. The tie between the strand ↦ parent-edge bijection and the visit identification of the word (strand along edge i carries visit (c,i)) is forced by geo_self_intersections clause 2 (GeoCarrierSelfIntersections.lean:767-775: the segment leaving visit w is a positive multiple of edge P w.2.val) plus transversality, but is not a field — non-blocking, as reviewer 3 labelled.

4. hn : 3 ≤ n (637). Not in the printed binder. But no Diagrammatic P exists for n ≤ 2: with Diagrammatic (Setup.lean:1382-1388), for n = 2 and P0 ≠ P1 every interior point of the segment has exactly the two preimages (0,λ),(1,1−λ), so selfIntersections is infinite (clause 2 fails); for n = 2 with P0 = P1 or n = 1 the single traced point has infinitely many preimages (clause 3 fails). So hn drops no printed instance — non-blocking (indeed vacuous).

5. Remaining fields: carriers_of_S (650) = lem:carriers (i); initial_carrier (653-655) = lem:carriers (iv) at S; step (659-662) and step_well_defined (665-668) render the statement's own route sentences (d1:599-601, 606-607) in universally quantified (stronger) form over all StepInvariant K and all carriers q — the 'hypotheses persist' content is a proof sentence but extra true content in a Prop bundle, non-blocking; the 'daughter' containment is the accepted CV.carrierword refinement clause (CarrierWord.lean:322-328), non-blocking; closed_plane_curve (677) is Regular ∧ Generic (LinkDiagram.lean:394-400: regular, tail_off immersion, transverse, no triple) — stronger than 'closed plane curve' and the proof's own 'closed plane curve with transverse double points' (d1:627-628); double_points (680-685) gives both the combinatorial and the traced-curve geometric form, matching 'double points are exactly the crossings of H'. Piece = connected component of the induced interlacement graph on U(S) (Carriers.lean:690-704), Ind/U/N (Events.lean:165-179) and Diagrammatic match the printed binder.
